standard_prerequisites.use: Turns purity into the statement that every relative associated point specializes into the fibre, describes the relative assassin after base changing to the henselization as an inverse image, and supplies the specialization criterion for purity that the converse must establish.

standard_prerequisites.name: Associated points of the pullback along an etale morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-etale-weak-assassin-up-down, invoked at proof line 5268 in the form applied to the morphism of fibres
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that a preimage of a relative associated point along the etale morphism g is again an associated point of the pulled back module on the corresponding fibre, which lets purity of the pullback be used to produce a specialization inside the fibre.

core_obligations: Reduce the base: since S' -> S is etale, purity of F along X_s implies purity of the pullback along X_s, and by flat descent of purity purity of the pullback along X'_{s'} implies purity of F along X_s; hence one may replace S by S' and further by its localisation at s, so that g : X' -> X is an etale morphism between finite type schemes over a local S (proof lines 5222-5233).

Forward direction: if F is pure along X_s then every relative associated point of F over S specializes to a point of X_s by purity, hence by the specialization lemma to a point of Ass_{X_s}(F_s), and therefore lies in the image of g because that image is open and contains Ass_{X_s}(F_s) (proof lines 5236-5244).

Converse: assume the image of g contains the relative associated points of F, base change along the henselization S^h of S at s using that the relative assassin is an inverse image, reducing to a henselian local base; then for a relative associated point x choose x' over it, note by the etale lemma applied to the morphism of fibres that x' is an associated point of the pulled back module, use that the pulled back module is pure along the fibre to produce a specialization x' to some y in that fibre, and push down to get x specializing to a point of X_s, which is the purity criterion (proof lines 5246-5272).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to S = S' with g etale between finite type schemes over a local base (proof lines 5222-5233).
Forward: purity forces relative associated points to specialize into the fibre and hence into the open image of g (proof lines 5236-5244).
Converse: base change to the henselization, lift the point along g, use purity of the pullback to specialize inside the fibre and push down (proof lines 5246-5272).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the purity criterion used throughout the chapter: under the standing hypotheses it says that F is pure along the fibre if and only if the image of the etale morphism contains the relative associated points of the pullback that specialize into the fibre (statement lines 5196-5219, tag 05L4). The proof reduces the base to the etale neighbourhood and its localisation, proves the forward direction through the specialization of associated points and the openness of the image of g, and then proves the converse by base changing to the henselization, lifting a relative associated point along the etale morphism via the associated point lemma for etale maps, and using purity of the pulled back module to produce the required specialization inside the fibre. The henselization step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
